newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says delays mobile phone bids results.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says delays mobile phone bids results.

text.p: Taiwan's Ministry of Transport and Communications said on Saturday that the hotly anticipated announcement of winners for lucrative mobile phone franchises due January 4 would be postponed.
The ministry said it required more time to review foreign investors' stakes in the applications.

"We have to delay the scheduled announcement today for the screening of results as we are uncertain about the exact stakes by foreign investors in these applications," Su Chung-hung, a ministry director in charge of the screening, told Reuters by telephone.

The mobile telephone sector is one of several telecom sectors liberalised by Taiwan's parliament in January 1996, opening them up for private and limited foreign investments. Foreign investors can own stakes of up to 20 percent in Taiwan telecom ventures.
Su said the problem now is resolving a definition of foreign investors because the ministry has said foreign investors do not include overseas Chinese in these applications.

"But the data we now have are figures that include both foreigners and overseas Chinese, so we cannot complete the final review unless we have the data separated into pure foreign investor holdings," Su said.
The ministry has yet to set an exact time to announce the results, he said. "But we will get these data as soon as possible, and complete the review and announce the results the soonest," Su said.

Seventeen joint ventures, some led by major international telecom firms, have submitted 42 applications to run the newly liberalised mobile telephone franchises that analysts say could yield up to US$3.6 billion a year in sales after 10 years.

The foreign and domestic applicants include AT&T, Sprint Corp, Southwestern Bell and Air Touch of the United States, Hong Kong Telecommunications, Japan's Mitsubishi as well as Acer and the influential Koo's Group of Taiwan.
